positiveFlows.title: HYDROPONIC FARMING IS A RAPIDLY GROWING METHOD FOR PRODUCING FRESH VEGETABLES, ESPECIALLY LETTUCE. HOWEVER, ONE OF THE BIGGEST CHALLENGES FACING GROWERS IS PYTHIUM ROOT ROT, A DISEASE THAT DAMAGES ROOTS, REDUCES YIELD, AND CAUSES SIGNIFICANT CROP LOSSES. CURRENT TOOLS TO DETECT AND MANAGE THIS DISEASE ARE LIMITED, AND GROWERS OFTEN LACK CLEAR GUIDANCE ON WHEN AND HOW TO INTERVENE. THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS TO HELP GROWERS PREVENT AND MANAGE PYTHIUM ROOT ROT. FIRST, WE WILL TRACK WHERE AND WHEN PYTHIUM OCCURS IN COMMERCIAL GREENHOUSES IN THE NORTHEAST AND MIDWEST. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP A RAPID DIAGNOSTIC TEST THAT ALLOWS GROWERS AND DIAGNOSTIC LABS TO DETECT THE PATHOGEN QUICKLY, MAKING IT EASIER TO RESPOND BEFORE LOSSES OCCUR. BY DETERMINING CRITICAL THRESHOLDS OF PYTHIUM THAT LEAD TO DISEASE, WE WILL HELP GROWERS KNOW WHEN IT IS MOST IMPORTANT TO TAKE ACTION. SECOND, WE WILL TEST BOTH COMMERCIAL AND NATURALLY OCCURRING BENEFICIAL MICROBES THAT MAY PROTECT PLANTS FROM ROOT ROT. THESE MICROBES COULD PROVIDE GROWERS WITH NEW OPTIONS TO REDUCE LOSSES AND IMPROVE ROOT HEALTH. WE WILL ALSO LEARN HOW APPLICATION METHODS AND TIMING AFFECT THE ABILITY OF THESE MICROBES TO SURVIVE IN HYDROPONIC SYSTEMS AND PROTECT CROPS. FINALLY, WE WILL WORK DIRECTLY WITH GROWERS TO SHARE WHAT WE LEARN. WE WILL OFFER WORKSHOPS, TRAINING PROGRAMS, AND GROWER CONSULTATIONS, SUPPORTED BY FACT SHEETS, TRADE MAGAZINE ARTICLES, AND ONLINE RESOURCES. GROWERS WHO PARTICIPATE WILL ALSO HAVE THE OPPORTUNITY TO TEST THEIR OWN SYSTEMS FOR PYTHIUM AND BENEFICIAL MICROBES, GAINING PRACTICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE BIOLOGY OF THEIR PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. TOGETHER, THESE EFFORTS WILL REDUCE CROP LOSSES, IMPROVE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, AND HELP ENSURE THE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF HYDROPONIC FARMING.

UNDERSTANDING HOW TO BUILD AND MAINTAINSUSTAINABLE URBAN SYSTEMS IS ONE OF THE GRAND CHALLENGES OF THE 21ST CENTURY. URBAN AGRICULTURE (UA) - PRODUCING FOOD IN (PERI)URBAN AREAS - HAS BEEN PROPOSED AS A PROMISING URBAN SUSTAINABILITY SOLUTION. YET CURRENT SUSTAINABILITY BENEFITS OF UA ARE CONSTRAINED DUE TO SMALL-SCALE IMPLEMENTATION, EVEN THOUGH MANY CITIES IN THE U.S. ARE EXPERIENCING INCREASING COMMUNITY INTERESTS, GRASSROOT AND POLICY SUPPORT FOR UA DEVELOPMENT. HENCE, IT IS CRUCIAL TO SCALE UP (BOOSTS IN NUMBER, CAPACITY, INFRASTRUCTURE) CURRENT UA PRODUCTION SYSTEMS TO FULLY REALIZE ITS IMPLICATIONS ON SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, IMPROVED KNOWLEDGE, APPROACH, AND SYSTEM FOR SITING NEW UA ARE REQUIRED IN WAYS THAT CAN COMPREHENSIVELY ACCOUNT FOR BIOPHYSICAL, INFRASTRUCTURAL, SOCIAL, AND ECONOMIC FACTORS. IN THIS INTEGRATED RESEARCH-EXTENSION PROJECT, WE AIM TO (1) DEVELOP A MULTI-CRITERIA DECISION ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL SITES FOR SCALING UP UA; AND (2) DESIGN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TECHNIQUES TO DETERMINE OPTIMAL LOCATIONS FOR UA NETWORK EXPANSION FOR INCORPORATING INTO A WEB-BASED DECISION SUPPORT TOOL. WE WILL FOCUS ON THREE EMERGING, INDOOR UAS WITH SUBSTANTIAL POTENTIALS FOR MASS AND COMMERCIALIZED PRODUCTION: VACANT LOT VERTICAL FARMS, ROOFTOP GREENHOUSES, AND FLOATING FARMS, BY USING GREATER MIAMI REGION AS A TEST BED. OUR FRAMEWORKCAN BE BROADLY APPLICABLE TO OTHER CITIES EXPERIENCING INTERESTS IN UA DEVELOPMENT. OUR FINDINGS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT, AND BE INCORPORATED INTO EXISTING STATEWIDE EXTENSION PROGRAMS TO GUIDE OPTIMIZED UA DEVELOPMENT TO ACHIEVE URBAN SUSTAINABILITY.

THIS PROJECT IS FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND TESTING A NEW PACKAGING TECHNOLOGY TO HELP FRUITS LAST LONGER AND STAY MOLD-FREE DURING STORAGE AND SHIPPING. THE WORK WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY RYP LABS OF BOTHELL, WASHINGTON, AND WILL TAKE PLACE IN FOUR MAJOR STAGES.THE FIRST STAGE WILL FOCUS ON CREATING AND IMPROVING METHODS NEEDED TO TEST AND BUILD THIS NEW TECHNOLOGY. THIS INCLUDES GATHERING MATERIALS AND DEVELOPING WAYS TO MEASURE HOW CERTAIN COMPOUNDS (LIKE 1-METHYLCYCLOPROPENE (1-MCP), A COMMON RIPENING INHIBITOR) ARE RELEASED FROM THE PACKAGING. WORK WILL ALSO COMMENCE ON CREATING SMALL PACKETS MADE FROM EITHER SALT-BASED OR GEL-LIKE MATERIALS THAT CAN SLOWLY RELEASE HELPFUL GASES TO PROTECT THE FRUIT. THE GOAL IS TO FINE-TUNE HOW THE MATERIALS ARE MADE SO THAT THEY RELEASE THE GASES IN A CONTROLLED WAY, BASED ON FACTORS LIKE HUMIDITY.THE SECOND STAGE WILL USE THE METHODS DEVELOPED IN THE FIRST STAGE TO BUILD REAL VERSIONS OF THESE PACKAGING MATERIALS. THESE SMALL PACKETS, KNOWN AS SACHETS, WILL BE TESTED IN LABORATORY CONDITIONS THAT MIMIC REAL STORAGE ENVIRONMENTS. THE GOAL HERE IS TO SEE HOW WELL THE SACHETS WORK AT DIFFERENT TEMPERATURES AND HUMIDITY LEVELS. PROJECT SCIENTISTS WILL MEASURE HOW FAST THE ACTIVE COMPOUNDS ARE RELEASED AND HOW CONSISTENTLY THE SACHETS PERFORM. THE MOST PROMISING DESIGNS WILL MOVE ON TO THE NEXT PHASE.THE THIRD STAGE FOCUSES ON TESTING THE MOST SUCCESSFUL SACHETS IN MORE REALISTIC SETTINGS, LIKE INSIDE REFRIGERATORS OR SHIPPING CONTAINERS THAT STORE FRUIT. THE GOAL IS TO CONFIRM THAT THE SACHETS RELEASE THE RIGHT AMOUNT OF RIPENING INHIBITOR AND ANTIFUNGAL AGENTS OVER TIME. THE TEAM WILL ALSO DO SOME SMALL-SCALE TASTE AND SMELL TESTS ON THE FRUIT TO MAKE SURE THE PACKAGING DOESN'T NEGATIVELY AFFECT QUALITY. THESE TESTS WILL HELP FURTHER REFINE THE PRODUCT.IN THE FINAL STAGE, THE MOST EFFECTIVE SACHET DESIGN WILL BE TESTED IN PARTNERSHIP WITH A RESEARCH LAB AT TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY. THESE TESTS WILL INVOLVE USING THE SACHETS WITH ACTUAL FRUIT, SUCH AS MANGOES AND AVOCADOS, STORED UNDER STANDARD SHIPPING AND STORAGE CONDITIONS. THE RESEARCHERS WILL LOOK AT HOW WELL THE SACHETS PREVENT MOLD AND SLOW DOWN RIPENING. THE TEAM WILL ALSO MEASURE THE TEXTURE AND QUALITY OF THE FRUIT. BASED ON THE RESULTS, THE PRODUCT MAY BE IMPROVED ONE LAST TIME BEFORE A FINAL VERSION IS CREATED AND A DETAILED REPORT IS WRITTEN ABOUT THE TECHNOLOGY'S POTENTIAL.IN SUMMARY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CREATE A SMART, HUMIDITY-SENSITIVE PACKAGING SOLUTION THAT HELPS EXTEND THE SHELF LIFE OF FRUIT BY SLOWING RIPENING AND PREVENTING MOLD, WHILE ENSURING THE FRUIT'S TASTE AND QUALITY REMAIN UNAFFECTED.

THE COMBINED EFFORTS OF GLOBAL NEIGHBOR INC. (GNI) IN COLLABORATION WITH TEXAS A&M UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP AND INTER-ROW DIRECTED ENERGY SYSTEM FOR NON-CHEMICAL WEED MANAGEMENT AND DESIGNATE IT AS THE DA-6NT. THE PROPOSED PROJECT SEEKS TO PROVE THE TECHNICAL AND COMMERCIAL FEASIBILITY OF A NOVEL NON-CHEMICAL WEED CONTROL TECHNOLOGY THAT BUILDS ON THE PRIOR WORK DONE BY TAMU AND GNI AND THAT WILL PROVIDE SMALL TO MEDIUM-SIZED ORGANIC GROWERS WITH HIGHER EFFICACY AND FLEXIBILITY IN THEIR PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. SMALL TO MID-SIZED ORGANIC STAKEHOLDERS ARE IN DIRE NEED OF AFFORDABLE, RESOURCE-EFFICIENT WEED MANAGEMENT TOOLS, AND THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO BEGIN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUCH A DEVICE THROUGH A MULTI-ORGANIZATIONAL COLLABORATION. THE COLLABORATION IS A STARTING POINT THAT WILL FOSTER FURTHER INNOVATIONS THROUGH THE COMBINED EFFORTS OF A LEADING WEED SCIENCE RESEARCH LABORATORY AT AN R1 (VERY HIGH RESEARCH ACTIVITY) UNIVERSITY, TEXAS A&M WITH A SMALL BUSINESS WITH ENGINEERING AND MARKET EXPERTISE (GLOBAL NEIGHBOR INC.).
